title: Declarative state-machine Terraform module for private EKS control plane provisioning and health orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a single, reusable Terraform module that manages the lifecycle of Redwood Private EKS control planes inside customer VPCs using a declarative state machine pattern. The module should make provisioning, upgrades, health checks, and rollback orchestration predictable and idempotent for both self-serve and managed customers.

Background: Current provisioning logic is split across bootstrappers and ad-hoc scripts with fragile upgrade paths. This leads to intermittent upgrade failures, long recovery windows, and unclear observability for control plane health (certificate rotations, etc.). We need a module that encodes state transitions (PROVISIONING -> HEALTHCHECK -> READY -> UPGRADE_PENDING -> UPGRADE_IN_PROGRESS -> ROLLBACK) and integrates with existing observability and KMS/hardening controls.

Scope: Implement Terraform module composed of: 1) declarative state resources (S3/dynamo state-locking optional), 2) idempotent provisioners for EKS control plane (control-plane IAM roles, endpoint config, security groups, CMK/KMS bindings), 3) health orchestration hooks (preflight, post-provision probes, certificate checks, snapshot triggers), 4) upgrade orchestration primitives (canary policy flags, paused rollouts, automatic fallback on health regression), 5) clear outputs and metrics integration (CloudWatch/Prometheus labels, audit log hooks). Module must be usable by both Redwood Private on VPC and on-prem orchestrator via wrappers.

Out-of-scope: worker node autoscaling, tenant-level app deployment, or control plane replacement strategies that require live traffic migration. Those will be handled by separate tickets.

Notes: We will avoid embedding procedural logic in remote-exec scripts; prefer Terraform provisioner minimalism plus a small, tested controller Lambda/StepFunction that drives complex transitions when needed. This keeps the module auditable and easy to reason about in customer repos.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Module can be applied idempotently to create a Private EKS control plane in a test VPC and transitions to READY with green health checks.
2) Module exposes outputs for control plane endpoint, cert rotation window, and health status resource.
3) Upgrade path: canary flag toggles a staged upgrade (10% -> 50% -> 100%) that will automatically stop and rollback if health probes fail for >2 minutes at any stage.
4) Preflight validations run and fail fast on missing IAM/KMS/SecurityGroup constraints with actionable error messages.
5) Integration tests: terraform apply/destroy passes in CI with mocked IAM creds and recorded API calls.
6) Documentation and an example consumer repo (private-provisioner-examples) demonstrating a canary upgrade and a forced rollback.
7) Security review completed and audit/event logs surface kube-apiserver trust changes.

rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge to canary branch and run CI e2e in staging account (1 day). Stage 2: Deploy module to internal managed customer demo accounts (2 days), monitor CloudWatch metrics and Console health dashboards. Stage 3: Enable canary upgrades for internal customers only for 2 weeks, evaluate health regressions and rollback events. Stage 4: General availability with documentation and console toggles. Rollback strategy: StepFunction signals ROLLBACK state, module issues snapshot and rolls control plane to previous stable config; notify on-call and create incident record.
